label: Private repos with a public page
means: Private repos whose GitHub Pages site is set public, or loads for a visitor who is signed out.
goal_source: template goal: a private repo shows nothing signed out; GitHub Docs, Changing the visibility of your GitHub Pages site (read 2026-11-19), lets a site be published privately instead
source: gh api orgs/<owner> and orgs/<owner>/repos, then repos/<repo>/pages of each private repo with a site, and one signed-out request to its html_url (collectors/visibility/visibility.mjs); not measured when the token cannot count every private repo

params.comment: owner: the GitHub org or personal account audited; empty means this repo's owner. A personal account is read through users/<owner> and user/repos, so it needs a login as that user. org_domains: email domains the org owns, beyond its profile's site and email domain, so an author at one is not personal. bot_emails: author addresses that are tools, not people, such as the one Claude Code cloud sessions commit as; an address listed is not personal. Setting it replaces the default, so keep noreply@anthropic.com in the list.

label: Public repos without secret scanning
means: Public, unarchived repos where secret scanning or push protection is off.
goal_source: GitHub Docs, About secret scanning (read 2026-11-19): on public repositories secret scanning runs automatically for free, so none has a reason to be off; push protection on too is this template's goal
source: security_and_analysis of each public, unarchived repo in gh api orgs/<owner>/repos (collectors/visibility/visibility.mjs); a token that gets none for any of them, as the workflow token may, leaves it not measured

label: Personal emails in public history
means: Distinct author emails in public history that are not noreply, a listed tool address or an owned domain.
goal_source: template goal: the commits API returns each author email to anyone; GitHub Docs, Setting your commit email address (read 2026-11-19), makes a no-reply address the author email once email privacy is on
source: gh api --paginate repos/<repo>/branches, then every commit of each branch, every page, of every public repo (collectors/visibility/visibility.mjs); detail counts per repo and the forks of those repos, never an address

label: One audit run
means: Seconds one run takes to read every repo of the org.
goal_source: template goal, no public benchmark: an org audit is one run that finishes within a minute, near five
source: wall time of collectors/visibility/visibility.mjs, from the org read to the last commit read

label: API requests per audit
means: gh api requests one audit run spends.
goal_source: goal a tenth, near a quarter, of the workflow token's limit: GitHub Docs, Rate limits for the REST API (read 2026-11-19), GITHUB_TOKEN gets 1,000 requests per hour per repository
source: gh api requests collectors/visibility/visibility.mjs made, one per page
